title: Meeting Conflicts
statement:
Decide whether one person can attend every meeting on a calendar.

Contract
- `meetings` is non-null, unsorted, and may be empty. Each meeting is `{start, end}` with
  `start < end`; values may be any `int`, including extreme ones.
- Meetings are half-open: `{start, end}` occupies `[start, end)`. A meeting that starts exactly
  when another ends does not conflict with it.
- Return `true` when no two meetings overlap, `false` otherwise. Identical meetings conflict.
- Do not mutate `meetings`.

Examples
- `canAttendAll({{9, 10}, {10, 11}, {13, 14}})` returns `true`.
- `canAttendAll({{1, 5}, {4, 8}})` returns `false`.
- `canAttendAll({})` returns `true`.
hints: If you looked at the meetings in calendar order, which pairs would you need to compare?
After sorting by start time, a conflict exists exactly when some meeting starts before the previous one ends. Adjacent pairs are enough.

Sort a copy by start with `Integer.compare`, then scan once, treating a start equal to the previous end as fine. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort and O(n) space, where n is the number of meetings.
